lead: WTI Crude / CL=F — The war premium drains out of oil
smaller: Robinhood / HOOD — The crowd's own broker hears silence
Rivian / RIVN — The EV upstart that kept its promise
Hims & Hers / HIMS — Telehealth's cheap growth stock promises profits
why_lead: Crude combined the day's clearest cross-asset move with a simple crowd story going wrong: WTI -4.27% to 77.37 USD/bbl and -10.00% over 20 sessions (below 85.97 on 2023-10-10), Brent -4.19%, SLB -5.58%, XLE -2.22%, while producers reported the damage (Aramco profit falls n1266, Kuwait deficit n1777) and supply headlines ran the other way (n1699, n0824). Attention evidence is the retail funnel built on war tensions: an oil-and-gas stock list for Q4 2023 (n0364), the Buffett energy pitch (n0708), Rigzone's most-mentioned-on-X list (n0576) and a conflict-and-oil explainer (n1734). The war fear itself is cited (n1375, n1366); the 1973 analog is named in n1696; smart-money split from J.P. Morgan (n0604), supermajor consolidation (n0629), BlackRock-Occidental (n0857) and OPEC-Brazil (n1779). Oil has not led or appeared in any earlier November edition.
why_smaller: Robinhood: newly published Q3 miss on muted trading activity (n1265) plus Coinbase volume decline (n0986), set against TQQQ +19.22% and ARKK +16.62% over five sessions; ETF-mainstreaming coverage (n1352, n1669) supplies the break. A retail-participation narrative distinct from oil, EVs and telehealth.

Rivian: newly published Q3 beat and raised production goal (n0913, n0914) against Lucid's forecast cut (n0898); demand-slowdown and price-war headlines (n1772, n0644) supply the break. An EV-shakeout-survivor narrative, distinct from the 2023-11-06 Tesla dip-buy item (different company, different catalyst).

Hims & Hers: +10.99% to 6.97 USD and +16.56% over five sessions on a raised revenue outlook with profitability expected in early 2024 (n0885) and a new product launch (n0777): a cheap-growth-stock profit-inflection narrative.
